sentences.english_text: Do you know who stopped World War III from happening?
That's right, Drippy.
All the yelling around him and the generals racing back and forth woke him up.
It's impossible to get any sleep around here.
Drippy grumbled.
He sat up and looked around.
I wonder what everyone is so excited about.
They're all running and yelling and carrying on like maniacs.
I'm going to have to find a quieter place to go to sleep.
And he slipped through a tiny crack in the computer.
The moment Drippy left the computer, it began to function normally again.
The warning bell stopped and the sirens stopped.
And the computers no longer showed that attacks were coming from the north and the south and the east and the west and from the air and the ground and the sea.
Look what's happened.
We weren't being attacked by the Russians.
The computers were wrong.
I must tell the Russians.
A general looked at a clock on the wall and said, It's too late, Mr. President.
There's only one minute left before the attack.
The president quickly picked up the hotline and said to the Russian, General, we're turning our planes back.
Will you turn yours back?
As soon as you do, the Russian replied.
The president gave an order.
Tell our planes to turn back.
And as they watched the map on the wall, they could see that their planes were turning back toward the United States.
Ten seconds later, the Russian planes turned back to Russia.
Everyone in the room gave a cheer.
As they started hugging each other and slapping one another on the back.
You've done it, the general said to the president.
You've stopped World War III.
But you and I know that it was Grippy who stopped World War III.
